title: AI-assisted_software_development
summary:
AI-assisted software development is the use of artificial intelligence to augment software development. It uses large language models, natural language processing, intelligent agents, and other AI technologies to assist software developers in a range of tasks of the software development life cycle, from initial code generation to subsequent debugging, testing, and documentation.

Key concepts include agentic coding, which denotes the use of more autonomous AI agents for software development; code generation, where LLMs trained on source code repositories generate functional code from natural language prompts; and code completion, where AI agents using pre-trained and fine-tuned LLMs predict and suggest code completions based on context, going beyond simple keyword matching to infer the developer's intent.

The outputs from AI-assisted software development require validation through a combination of automated testing, static analysis tools, and human review, creating a governance layer that acts as a safeguard ensuring quality and accountability. AI is also used to automatically generate test cases, identify potential bugs, suggest fixes, perform static code analysis, identify security vulnerabilities, suggest performance improvements, and ensure adherence to coding standards.

Vibe coding is a related software development practice in which a developer describes a project or task in a prompt to a large language model, which generates source code automatically. The term was coined by Andrej Karpathy, a co-founder of OpenAI and former AI leader at Tesla, in February 2025. In March 2025, Y Combinator reported that 25% of startup companies in its Winter 2025 batch had codebases that were 95% AI-generated. Notably, experienced open-source developers were found to be 19% slower when using AI coding tools, despite predicting they would be 24% faster and still believing afterward they had been 20% faster.
